headline: Trail Shelter and Litchfield Hills Lodging Check
reservation: No permits are required for day hiking or using the primitive AT shelters, which operate on a first-come basis. However, boutique inns in Kent and Salisbury require booking months in advance for the October foliage peak. Check the Appalachian Trail Conservancy for seasonal shelter closures or maintenance alerts before starting a multi-day hike.

days.title: River Valleys and Covered Bridges

stops.name: Bulls Bridge
stops.detail: View the historic covered bridge and the powerful Housatonic River cascades where the trail crosses the water.

stops.name: Housatonic River Walk
stops.detail: Enjoy a flat, five-mile stretch of the AT that follows the riverbank, ideal for bird watching.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes between trailheads; roads are paved but winding in the river valley.
days.note: This section can be muddy after heavy rain; sturdy footwear is recommended even for the flat portions.

days.title: The High Peaks of Connecticut

stops.name: Bear Mountain Summit
stops.detail: Climb the highest peak in Connecticut for a view that spans three states from the stone cairn.

stops.name: Sage's Ravine
stops.detail: Descend into this lush, hemlock-shaded gorge featuring waterfalls and moss-covered rocks.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes to reach the Undermountain Trailhead; parking is limited on weekends.
days.note: The climb to Bear Mountain is steep and rocky; allow extra time for the descent through the ravine.

days.title: Ridgelines and Vistas

stops.name: Rand's View
stops.detail: Walk through an open meadow for one of the most famous panoramic vistas of the Berkshires.

stops.name: Pine Knob Loop
stops.detail: Hike this trail for elevated views of the Housatonic Valley and the town of Cornwall.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes travel; local roads are narrow and require caution during winter or wet weather.
days.note: Hunting season occurs in the surrounding forests during fall; hikers should wear blaze orange as a precaution.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Small dirt lots at Undermountain and Bulls Bridge fill rapidly on autumn weekends. Have a secondary hike planned in case your primary trailhead parking is full, and avoid parking on narrow road shoulders.

intel.title: Litchfield Hills Reception
intel.text: Signal is generally strong in the towns of Kent and Salisbury but becomes highly unreliable in the deep ravines. Do not rely on digital maps for navigation once you leave the river valley for the high ridges.

intel.title: Village Services
intel.text: Fuel and basic supplies are easily found in the centers of Kent and Salisbury. Outside these village hubs, there are no services directly on the trail or along the secondary forest roads.

intel.title: Foliage and Mud Season
intel.text: Late September to mid-October is peak foliage, bringing the largest crowds to the vistas. Late spring (May and June) offers blooming mountain laurel but requires checking for 'mud season' trail closures.

intel.title: Terrain Difficulty
intel.text: The CT section varies from flat river walks to strenuous rock scrambles on the northern peaks. Match your route to your physical condition, as some descents are very taxing on the knees.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Bradley International (BDL) and drive west through New Hartford. Stop in Kent for local groceries and hiking supplies before heading to your inn or trailhead.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the main roads connecting the gateway towns. Many trailheads are accessed via well-maintained gravel roads that do not require 4WD under normal conditions.
plan.goldenHour: Rand’s View provides a classic New England meadow sunset, looking west toward the rolling peaks of the Berkshires.
